Hi Sarah / Tom '

Thanks again for the time today 'really helpful to hear more about Acme's checkout assistant and the traffic profile. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can align on a dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive):

Recap from today
- Primary use-case: generative assistant for checkout & post-purchase support (intent detection, multi-turn clarifications, text generation for upsell).
- Current traffic (high level): bursts during promo windows, steady baseline during business hours.
- Primary success criteria: p95 latency <= 700ms on user-facing responses; predictable throughput during promotional spikes; data isolation for PII.

What we'd like to cover in the sizing call
- Target throughput and concurrency (QPS / concurrent sessions) across peaks vs baseline
- Typical request size (avg / 95th tokens in / out) and prompt templates
- Latency SLOs and acceptable trade-offs (quantization, batching, caching)
- Network topology and egress constraints (for Private/Dedicated deployment)

Proposed next step
- Schedule a 60-minute dedicated capacity sizing call (technical deep dive) with your engineering + our SE team (Priyom). During the call we'll review traffic samples and propose a Dedicated config (GPU pool sizing, batching, and KV caching strategy).

Proposed times (PST):
- Wed, Dec 2 ' 10:00' 11:00 AM PST
- Thu, Dec 3 ' 2:00' 3:00 PM PST
Please let me know which slot works, or share a couple of preferred times and we'll send a calendar invite.

Prep items that will speed the call
- Recent traffic export (CSV) showing requests/minute, avg tokens in/out, and p95 latency ' sample attached as "sample-traffic-export.csv".
- Short network diagram or notes on proxy/egress restrictions.
- Example prompts (1–2 per main intent).

Attaching a short agenda (capacity-sizing-agenda.pdf). Priyom will join to drive the technical portion. Vivek is cc'd for deal context.

Cheers,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142
Redwood Inference
